# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_GET_ADDRESS_BOOK_ENTRY::response_t,
#         src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:2006-2013 -> { entries[] = entry (:1993-2004) }
#         entry = { index u64, address string, description string }
# NO status/untrusted.
# request: { entries[] list<u64> } (:1983-1990); an EMPTY list means all of them, which is what
#         fmonero sends.
# METHOD NAME: the struct is COMMAND_RPC_GET_ADDRESS_BOOK_ENTRY (singular ENTRY) but the wire method
#         -- and this file's name -- is `get_address_book`. Likewise add_address_book and
#         delete_address_book against ..._ADD_ADDRESS_BOOK_ENTRY / ..._DELETE_ADDRESS_BOOK_ENTRY.
#         Fixture names are wire names.
# THIS FILE DRIVES @label RESOLUTION, step 5a of §2a.1's refusal order. `wallet send @exchange 0.1`
#         runs ONE get_address_book on the open wallet and matches CASE-INSENSITIVELY against
#         `description`. The four rows below are chosen so all three outcomes are reachable from one
#         fixture, which is the only way a stateless mock can drive them:
#           @cold      -> zero matches                 -> exit 6 not_found
#           @savings   -> exactly one (index 0)        -> resolves to that address
#           @exchange  -> TWO (index 1 "Exchange" and index 2 "exchange", equal case-insensitively)
#                                                      -> exit 7 ambiguous, listing both
#           @donations -> exactly one (index 3)        -> resolves
#         The Exchange/exchange pair is deliberate: the case-insensitive rule is what makes them
#         collide, and without a colliding pair exit 7 has no input and the rule is untested.
# THE RESOLVED ADDRESS -- NEVER THE LABEL -- is what Plan.dest, every line send::relay announces, the
#         pending.json record and §5c's `dest` key carry (§4). A label in any of those would put a
#         name where an audit needs an address.
# A BARE WORD IS NEVER GUESSED AT AS A LABEL: only an @-prefixed dest reaches this call (§4), and
#         step 2 of the refusal order skips address::parse for such a dest rather than failing it 15.
# addresses are real, checksum-valid mainnet vectors from upstream's own test suite:
#         index 0 and 3: tests/functional_tests/validate_address.py:69 and :74
#         index 1 and 2: tests/unit_tests/base58.cpp:470 and
#                        tests/unit_tests/address_from_url.cpp:40
#         All four are mainnet, matching get_address.json's wallet, so a resolved label survives the
#         §2a.6 nettype check.
# `index` IS THE HANDLE `wallet book remove INDEX` TAKES, and it is the row's position in wallet2's
#         own vector -- deleting a row RENUMBERS the ones after it. Nothing in this fixture set can
#         show that (the mock is stateless), so a test that removes and then re-reads is a RED row.
